news.headline: uniQure Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Company Update
news.summary: uniQure reported Q2 2026 revenue of $5.8 million and a net loss of $81.1 million, ending the quarter with $810.3 million in cash after the June offering, enough to fund operations into 2030. The company confirmed both the US BLA and UK MHRA marketing authorization application for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease remain on track for submission in Q3 2026.

news.headline: Wolfe Research Upgrades uniQure (QURE) to Outperform, $65 Price Target
news.summary: Wolfe Research raised its rating on uniQure from Peer Perform to Outperform with a $65 price target, citing a roughly 70% probability of success for AMT-130 and projecting about $2 billion in peak US sales. The upgrade came the same day as uniQure's Q2 earnings release.

news.headline: uniQure CMO Signals FDA Advisory Committee Likely for AMT-130
news.summary: On the Q2 earnings call, chief medical officer Walid Abi-Saab said an FDA advisory committee meeting is likely for AMT-130 since it would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease, adding the company is preparing for one. uniQure also said it plans to present four-year follow-up data on all 24 patients from the first two AMT-130 dosing cohorts in September 2026.

news.headline: uniQure CEO Matthew Kapusta Sells Shares After Option Exercise Under 10b5-1 Plan
news.summary: CEO Matthew Kapusta exercised options for 21,082 shares at $19.39 and sold the same number at an average of $45.16 under a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 plan, worth about $952,000. uniQure's CMO also sold 30,000 shares on June 30 under a similar plan, while a JPMorgan Chase 13G filing disclosed a new roughly 7% passive institutional stake around the same time.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Preliminary Data on First Cohort of Phase I/IIa AMT-260 Trial in Refractory Epilepsy
news.summary: As of a May 29, 2026 data cutoff, three of six patients in the low-dose cohort of the AMT-260 epilepsy gene therapy trial achieved seizure reductions of 79% to 100% during months four through six of follow-up, with the therapy generally well tolerated and no serious related adverse events. uniQure said a second, higher-dose cohort is enrolling with updated data from both cohorts expected in the first half of 2027.

news.headline: uniQure to Seek Accelerated FDA Approval for AMT-130 After FDA Reversal, Shares Surge
news.summary: The FDA reversed course and told uniQure that 3-year Phase I/II data can support an accelerated-approval BLA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, sending shares up more than 70% in premarket trading. uniQure said it plans to submit the BLA in Q3 2026 and launched a $150 million public offering (later upsized to roughly $259 million) to fund commercialization readiness and the required confirmatory study.

catalysts.label: FDA BLA submission for AMT-130
catalysts.detail: uniQure remains on track to submit a Biologics License Application seeking accelerated approval of AMT-130 for Huntington's disease, following FDA agreement that 3-year Phase I/II data can support the filing; not yet submitted as of the July 29 earnings update.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA marketing authorization application for AMT-130
catalysts.detail: In parallel with the US filing, uniQure plans to submit a Marketing Authorization Application to the UK's MHRA for AMT-130, following a successful pre-submission meeting.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 four-year Phase I/II data presentation
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to present four-year follow-up safety and efficacy data on all 24 patients (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose) from the first two AMT-130 dosing cohorts in the Huntington's disease program.

catalysts.label: FDA Advisory Committee (AdCom) meeting for AMT-130
catalysts.detail: uniQure's chief medical officer said an FDA advisory committee meeting is likely for AMT-130 given it would be the first Huntington's disease gene therapy, and the company is preparing for one; no date has been set.

catalysts.label: Confirmatory study design alignment with FDA
catalysts.detail: uniQure is finalizing with the FDA the design of the required post-approval confirmatory study for AMT-130, including consideration of a concurrent standard-of-care control arm.

catalysts.label: Updated AMT-260 Phase I/IIa epilepsy data readout
catalysts.detail: uniQure expects to present updated safety and efficacy results, including higher-dose cohort data, from the ongoing AMT-260 refractory epilepsy trial.

pulse: uniQure is riding a strong rally since mid-June, when the FDA reversed course and agreed that 3-year AMT-130 data can support an accelerated-approval BLA for Huntington's disease; the company reaffirmed on its July 29 Q2 2026 earnings call that both the US BLA and a parallel UK MHRA filing remain on track for Q3 2026, with four-year data due in September 2026 and an FDA advisory committee meeting now considered likely. A $259 million equity offering completed in June pushed cash to $810.3 million, extending runway into 2030, while Wolfe Research upgraded shares to Outperform with a $65 target on AMT-130's commercial potential; early AMT-260 epilepsy data added a second pipeline catalyst, even as the CEO and CMO continued routine 10b5-1 share sales.
